blocks.x: Say, mom, what about the, uh, some of that stuff about the Lions Club and some of that stuff, you know?

Yeah, well, we had the Lions Club. Yeah. Well, we had the Olympic band then at the Lions Club. Well, that was also, uh, Talbot was in there then. And in other words, everybody knew him, like, call him Cuckoo. They knew Talbot by that means. And, uh, he used to sing, uh, Louis Armstrong's song a lot, and everybody really thought, sometimes people in the dance would say, uh, Louis Armstrong sang, uh, about, uh, if you be my baby, uh, the Butter and Eggman, you know? Mm-hmm. That song?
I want a big Butter and Eggman.

Yeah. Come be my, no, I'll be, uh, Butter and Eggman. Well, two, three people used to think, he was saying that so good, Talbot, you know, which was Cuckoo. He, uh, a lot of people would come to us and say, that's the Butter and Eggman? So we'd say, yeah, that's the Butter and Eggman. And he used to go around advertising trucks, you know, in our trucks, uh, them furniture waves. When he was gonna have a dance like at the Lions Club or Santa Centers. Well, most times they'd have two bands. They'd have René, you know, Kid René at the Santa Centers. Well, Kid René played, uh, trumpet. And his brother played, uh, Joe René played, uh, drum. You know. And, uh, Richard was, and I'd swap over, I think he was with Kid René there one time. But, uh. He was, yeah.
He told me he was, yes. Yeah.
When he was playing banjo then.
